item.title: 2026 Metrotrails Musikfest Night Hike / Explore — Thu Aug 6, 4:00 PM
item.description:
Metrotrails: NJ, PA, NY Metropolitan Area Hiking and More! Join us for an evening of night hiking in and around Musikfest in Bethlehem, PA.
Going back to my 2024 route, starting in Monocacy Park, heading South along the creek for some gorgeous woods and cold, clean swim spots. We will visit North side of Musicfest for some drinks and food and then wander along the cemetery full of Ginko trees, down to the abandoned CNJ tracks, then across the river to South side. We'll probably do the trail along South side, maybe get the view from the parking deck, and then wander back North. Music, drinks, and food available for purchase.
Monocacy Park parking:
https://maps.app.goo.gl/69qwCWow2DJh4Hr96
About 10 miles, mostly flat, dogs are permitted at Musikfest. Bring a headlamp and swimming attire.
Message me if you have any questions! Hope to see you Thursday!
-Cupcake
Source: Meetup: Metrotrails Hiking

item.title: Young Innovators STEM Program — Wed Aug 12, 5:00 PM — Kidville Montclair
item.description: Young Innovators is a hands-on STEM program designed for students in grades 3rd – 7th who are curious, creative, and excited to explore the worlds of engineering and technology. It will be a 2-week program, and it is $60/week. Week 1 will be ‘Engineering in Action,’ where students take on engaging engineering challenges through LEGO design, bridge-building competitions, and Rube Goldberg machine projects. Along the way, they learn how engineers use creativity, critical thinking, and problem-solving to develop solutions for real-world challenges. Week 2 will be ‘Coding and Game design,’ where students dive into computer science by learning the fundamentals of coding while designing and creating their own video games. This experience introduces programming concepts in a fun, interactive, and accessible way. item.title: Virtual Meditation — Wed Aug 12, 7:00 PM
item.description:
Summer session: July 1, 8, 22, 29. August 5, 12, 19 Wednesdays, 7:00 PM – 9:00 PM Join contemporary spiritual teacher and author Ramananda John E. Welshons (One Soul, One Love, One Heart, When Prayers Aren’t Answered and Awakening From Grief) for evening meditation classes in the comfort of your own home via Zoom. These classes will focus on specific practices for working with fear and anxiety. Participants will learn and practice different forms of mindfulness meditation in each session and will have the opportunity to participate in discussions of Ramananda’s three critically acclaimed books. Open to beginners and experienced practitioners, these gatherings offer an opportunity to experience deep inner peace while practicing with a highly experienced meditation teacher. item.description:
Calling all Montclair State faculty, staff, and students—it’s time to be a hero! Join us for our Blood Drive in proud partnership with the American Red Cross and help make a life-saving impact. Whether you’re a first-time donor or a seasoned pro, your donation can help replenish critical blood supplies used in emergencies, surgeries, and more. It’s quick, easy, and one of the most meaningful ways to give back to your community. So roll up your sleeve, grab a friend, and join us in turning compassion into action—because every drop counts. Snacks, smiles, and gratitude await! Donors also get an exclusive American Cross X Hello Kitty collectable item, while supplies last. RSVPing on Engage does not mean you are registered to donate. You must click and follow the link below in order to register as a donor for the drive! https://www.redcrossblood.org/give.html/drive-results?zipSponsor=Redhawk

item.title: Council On Ministries- Multi Platform — Tue Sep 8, 7:00 PM — UUCM-1-Peierls (60) [Multiplatform]
item.description: The UUCM Council on Ministries (CoM) exists to report to UUCM, its Board and Co-Ministers on how our programs are accomplishing their particular mission while also furthering the broader mission of UUCM. Special attention is paid to any systemic or cultural obstacles hindering our ability to fulfill our mission as well as any conflicts. Its primary goals are to maintain UUCM's Mission & Vision, restore trust and relationship when frayed, and to keep all our interactions in line with UUCM's covenant. Best practices, connectivity, cross-pollination and successes are also reported. The CoM also provides assistance evaluating our ministries periodically at the discretion of the Board. Please welcome Council on Ministries liaisons into your meetings and planning when they request to observe your functioning; share with them also your minutes and other documents when requested. They are charged by the Board to help us have a broad view of our function as it relates to living out our mission

item.title: SMC Trail Work Volunteer Day — Sun Sep 13, 9:00 AM
item.description:
South Mountain Conservancy Activities Meetup Group **TRAIL WORK will continue rerouting the Hogenauer Trail** (we are making progress!) up the slope and away from recently installed property fences. **Meet At:** Dog Park/ Wildflower Preserve, 11 Bear Lane, Maplewood. From there, we will walk to Crater View on Crest drive and then to the Hogenauer trail work site. (Note: While we normally meet the first Sudnay of each month, this volunteer day was shifted after the Labor Day weekend.)
Trail work is physically challenging but very satisfying as we use hand tools to build and repair trails. Participants must be 15+ years. Those younger than 18 must be accompanied by an adult. Participants **should wear long pants** due to [ticks](https://www.somocon.org/?page_id=193928&fb) and thron bushes and sturdy shoes, and bring gloves (though backup gloves will be available). item.title: Life Long Learning: Mary Cassatt: Impressionist Painter and Printmaker with Janet Mandel — Wed Sep 23, 1:00 PM — JCC MetroWest | Maurice Levin Theater
item.description:
In 2026, not only are we celebrating the 250th anniversary of the birth of the USA, but also the 100th anniversary of the death of artist Mary Cassatt. Janet Mandel will discuss how Cassatt, the only American among the Impressionists, has secured her place as a celebrated American icon. About the speaker: Janet Mandel retired after teaching for 32 years in the New Jersey public schools. She now presents illustrated lectures on art history at museums, adult schools, libraries, and senior centers. FREE for JCC Member; $15 Nonmember
Register Here
Sponsored by:
DAY TRIP On Thursday, October 15, join us for a docent-led Impressionism and Beyond tour at the Philadelphia Museum of Art, featuring seven Mary Cassatt paintings. The trip will include admission to the Marcel Duchamp retrospective as well, a perfect complement to Janet’s March 2025 lecture.

item.description: UNRECYCLABLE: Look Again – Assemblage Art by Andrew Borg Opening Reception: Friday, August 14, 5 – 8pm The Space presents Unrecyclable: Look Again, a solo exhibition of assemblage art by Andrew Borg composed predominantly of the unrecyclable plastics, foams, and composites he refused to throw away for nearly two years — the molded trays, caps, and packaging inserts that carry no recycling code and vanish into the trash without a thought. The exhibition, culminating Borg’s year as Artist in Residence at The Space, is on view August 14–22, 2026, with an opening reception Friday, August 14, from 5 to 8pm. What began as an act of defiance gradually became an act of appreciation: these are highly engineered, purpose-built objects, molded to cushion, position, and protect — aesthetic objects in their own right, designed by someone, meant to be forgotten by everyone.
